sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 46.6% a year from $6.91 billion in FY2017 to $215.9 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F211].
The path was not smooth: revenue fell 6.8% in FY2020 and grew just 0.2% in FY2023, then jumped 125.9% in FY2024 and 114.2% in FY2025 [D130][D284][D338][D393].
The FY2024 step change came from Data Center revenue up 217%, driven by Hopper GPU shipments for LLM training and inference [P22][P23].
FY2026 growth of 65.5% was driven by data center compute and networking platforms, with Blackwell the majority of Data Center revenue [D448][P10].
Data Center was 89.7% of FY2026 revenue and contributed 60.2pp of the 65.5% growth [D620][D622][D448].
Within it, Data Center computing grew 59% on Blackwell demand and Data Center networking grew 142% on NVLink for GB200 and GB300 systems [P8].
Operating costs grew 24.8pp slower than revenue in FY2026, at 40.7%, and incremental operating margin was 57.3% [D476][D468][D475].
Net income grew 64.7% against revenue growth of 65.5%, while diluted EPS grew 66.7% as the diluted share count fell 1.2% [D450][D448][D452][D470].
Growth is now concentrated in one platform and two direct customers representing 22% and 14% of revenue, so the top line carries customer-concentration risk [P6].
Operating margin of 60.4% in FY2026 sits well above the 32.8% window median but below the 62.4% FY2025 high [F50][D813][D812].
Gross margin fell 3.9pp to 71.1%, the cost-of-revenue line taking 3.9pp off operating margin, while R&D and SG&A added 1.3pp and 0.6pp [D462][F30][D477][D478][D479].
The FY2026 cost-of-revenue drag included a $4.5 billion H20 excess inventory and purchase obligation charge in the first quarter [P7].
In FY2026 net margin of 55.6% sat 4.8pp below the 60.4% operating margin, with other income of $11.1 billion partly offset by a 15.1% tax rate [F70][F50][X120][D434].
Other income rose on unrealized gains in non-marketable and publicly-held equity securities, including the Intel stake [P3].
Operating cash flow of $102.7 billion was 0.86x net income in FY2026, below the 1.00x of FY2017, and free cash flow was 0.81x [F100][F60][D435][D8][D436].
Free cash flow margin of 44.8% is near the 44.4% window median, with capex at 2.8% of revenue and 2.13x D&A [D432][D822][D431][D437].
Receivables grew 66.8% and inventory 112.3%, lifting days sales outstanding to 65 and days inventory to 125 [D473][D474][D445][D446].
Conversion at 0.86x reflects working capital absorbing cash as the balance sheet scales, not a deterioration in earnings quality [D435].
Net cash fell to $2.14 billion, or 1.0% of revenue, from $34.7 billion in FY2025, as cash and investments dropped 75.5% to $10.6 billion [D441][D442][D386][D471][D439].
Investing cash outflow of $52.2 billion rose on higher purchases of equity investment securities and a non-exclusive license agreement with Groq [F120][P1].
Net cash of 1.0% of revenue still ranks at the 83rd percentile of six semis peers against a -13.9% median, and the current ratio is 3.91x [D442][D844][D845][F190].
Buybacks and dividends of $41.1 billion were 42.5% of free cash flow, and return on average equity was 101.5% [D443][D444][D447].
Graphics was 44.1% of revenue and fell 25.0% in FY2023, a one-period decline [R1][D753][D754].
That episode is now historical, with Graphics at 10.4% of FY2026 revenue, so it does not describe the current business [D746].
Product revenue members tagged on one axis sum to 190% of consolidated revenue in FY2026 because some members are totals of others [R2].
Product-level shares must be read individually rather than added, which limits how finely the revenue mix can be decomposed.
If gross margin in the FY2027 10-K falls below the 71.1% of FY2026, the cost-of-revenue trend would confirm rather than reverse [F30].
If net cash as a share of revenue stays below the 1.0% of FY2026, the investing outflow would be outpacing cash generation [D442].
If operating cash flow to net income in the FY2027 10-K recovers above the 0.86x of FY2026, working capital absorption would be easing [D435].
